prompt:
A flat, matte design sketch of a desktop website homepage, landscape 16:9, shown straight on with no perspective, no device frame, no browser chrome, no drop shadows, no gloss, no photorealism. Deliberately unfinished, like a designer's layout study rendered in flat color blocks.

Palette, used exactly: warm aged-paper off-white background (#F7F3ED), dark warm ink for text (#2A231C), one muted slate blue accent used sparingly (#365778). No other colors. A very faint regular dot grid sits over the paper background.

Layout, top to bottom:

A thin quiet header strip across the very top, holding a few small greeked navigation items on the right. Keep it understated.

Below it, a large serif headline set across the left two thirds, reading exactly: Play a story in any world you can imagine

Under the headline, two short lines of greeked body text, then a single solid slate-blue rectangular button. To its right, a plain text link. These are the only strongly colored elements on the page.

Then the main event, filling the lower two thirds: a tall single column of body text occupying the left two thirds of the page, set as a serif reading column at comfortable book measure. All of this text is greeked: soft indistinct horizontal lines standing in for words, not real letters. It should read unmistakably as a long passage of prose, dense and continuous.

In the right third, an outer margin column holding three small notes, spaced far apart vertically so each sits beside a different part of the prose column. Each note is two or three short greeked lines set in a small monospace-looking style. From each note, a thin hairline rule runs left and touches a specific line in the prose column, like an annotation keyed to that line. One of the touched lines in the prose is subtly underlined or marked in the slate blue accent.

The word Narraitor appears once, small, in the header. Apart from that word and the headline, absolutely no legible text anywhere: every other text region is greeked indistinct lines. Do not render invented prices, dates, statistics, logos, faces, or photographs.

The overall feeling is a printed page from a well-set book with scholarly marginal notes, not a marketing website.
